answer: Like a wharf that only berths ships flying a beacon it has verified, an agent marketplace can require each identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed if the agent misbehaves. Newcomers start at the jetty with tiny transaction limits and earn larger limits only through a history of honest work. A Sybil attacker must therefore fund and risk a separate stake for every fake identity, so creating thousands of sock puppets costs thousands of stakes while honest agents pay only once.
